title: Deployment entitlement and fast-rollback protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we expand canary, A/B and shadowing capabilities, teams need a clear entitlement + approval flow that balances speed of iteration with safety. Current ad-hoc signoffs lead to long waits for low-risk changes and insufficient oversight for high-risk model swaps. This ticket defines the product-facing workflow, role mappings, audit expectations, and the fast auto-rollback protocol tied to observable SLO regressions. Scope: product rules, UI affordances for signoff, audit event schema, integrations with RBAC and SIEM, and failure modes (emergency bypass, escalation). Out of scope: low-level kernel scheduling and per-model compilation changes (handled in ENG backlog).
rollout_strategy: Phase 1: Canary (0.5% -> 5%), monitored by latency and correctness slices. Phase 2: Shadow traffic for new decoder variants at 10% mirrored load for 48h. Phase 3: Controlled A/B experiments with traffic split and user cohorting. Auto-rollback triggers evaluated continuously; manual gating required for >20% traffic moves. Entitlement model uses role tiers (requester, reviewer, approver, auditor) and rule sets per change criticality level.
rollback_thresholds: API error rate delta: +3 percentage points absolute within 10 minutes on canary traffic
P95 latency increase: +25% compared to baseline for 10 minutes
Quality regression: model-quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) relative drop >4% on monitored prompt set
Business KPI degradation signal from dashboard (e.g., conversion drop) flagged by ops
acceptance_criteria: Entitlement matrix published and accessible in Console with role mappings (requester, reviewer, approver, auditor)
UI changes show required signoffs for change criticality and surface outstanding approvals before rollout can start
Backend emits structured audit events for every lifecycle action (request/create/approve/reject/rollback) and events are ingested by SIEM endpoint
Auto-rollback pipeline implemented: metric ingest -> detector rules -> rollback API call -> rollback confirmation event
Emergency bypass workflow documented with two-person emergency approval and audit trail
End-to-end test simulating canary failing metric triggers automatic rollback in staging

audit_retention_policy: Audit events retained for 3 years in write-once encrypted store; 90-day hot window for Console UI and exports to SIEM. Access logs forwarded to security-analytics cluster.
escalation_path: Auto-rollback triggers append alert to oncall channel and create incident ticket. If rollback fails, escalate to SRE manager and open emergency approval flow requiring two approvers from oncall+engineering manager.
notes_on_tradeoffs: We favor faster rollouts for low-criticality models (auto-approve by default) but require human-in-the-loop for high-criticality changes. Trade-off: strict gating increases time-to-deploy but reduces blast radius. Auto-rollback thresholds tuned conservatively to avoid noisy rollbacks; may require manual intervention for subtle quality regressions.
